chunks.title: Replace jQuery with a vanilla client boundary
acceptance_criteria: The frontend has no jQuery runtime dependency or CDN requirement
Small vanilla modules separate API requests, local UI state, and rendering without a build step
Existing board loading and move submission behavior remains functional through the stable API envelope
Dependency policy, usage, security, and documentation records remove jQuery consistently

chunks.title: Build account game creation and history views
acceptance_criteria: A guest can start an untimed game quickly with sensible default labels
Registration, login, logout, account switching, preset/custom time controls, and validation feedback are usable without page-level alerts
Logged-in users can list and open only their personal saved games
Replay navigation steps through immutable saved positions while clearly separating review from the live game

chunks.title: Implement accessible board interaction and state cues
acceptance_criteria: Pieces move through drag/drop and click/tap source-destination interaction with keyboard-operable equivalents
Selection and legal destinations use server-provided data and promotion offers all four orthodox choices
Active side, last move, checked king, captures, orientation, and final position are visually and semantically distinct
Illegal attempts preserve the rendered canonical position and explain rejection non-disruptively

chunks.title: Present clocks controls and responsive terminal feedback
acceptance_criteria: Both clocks display server-owned state and the active clock advances visually without becoming authoritative
New game, reset/abandon, resign, draw offer/accept/claim, sound, and orientation controls reflect their allowed states
Checkmate, stalemate, timeout, resignation, agreed draw, and other draws receive distinct concise feedback
The board, controls, history, and status remain usable at representative laptop and mobile viewport sizes

chunks.title: Add local sound feedback and browser smoke coverage
acceptance_criteria: Local lightweight sounds distinguish move, capture, check, and game end and fail safely when audio is unavailable
One obvious sound control persists its preference in browser storage
Animation and sound never delay persistence, hide the final position, or block immediate controls
Repository-owned browser smoke coverage exercises guest play, account navigation, timed status, replay, responsive layout, and sound toggling
